proof_attempt_summary: Discovery informally proved 11 statements and verified two primary-source citations for the all-adaptive three-regime frontier and exact zero-risk threshold T=k+1. The independent math and terminal audits found the result sound, but novelty was incremental with ceiling 5.7 below the field floor 7.4 and no bounded same-topic repair. tldr: The published one-wave DTE minimax bound gap closes on balanced complete multipartite graphs under the identical normalized moment-two ANI class. Its sharp risk order is \((k-1)/k\), even when the published lower expression vanishes as the part size grows. With the same fixed response table reused after exact resets, the full all-adaptive frontier is \((k-T)/(kT)\) for \(T<k\), \(1/\{k\max(k,m)\}\) for \(T=k\), and zero exactly when \(T\ge k+1\). Finite nonadaptive schedules attain these orders against every original-record adaptive procedure. The complete stopped-record converse prices both omitted parts and unresolved arms, yielding the critical part-size transition and a necessary-and-sufficient consistency criterion. This is a prospective benchmark for direct-effect experiment planning on the proved graph family.
gap: Kandiros, Harshaw and S\"avje (2026), Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5, reduce a single network experiment to exposure sampling. Their lower bounds do not price the cumulative union of stable endpoints when later assignments can depend on full earlier outcomes. Ordinary survey theory supplies the missing-part component but does not resolve the coupled missing-part and missing-arm choice at \(T=k\).
fill: A complete-record sequential minimax reduction, observable finite schedules, and a general-policy uncertainty certificate lead to an explicit matched all-budget precision theorem. The zero-risk boundary and primitive consistency criterion are consequences of the same certificate, not separate unrelated projects.
